name: Charleston International Airport
before:
South Carolina's busiest airport, about 12 miles north west of downtown Charleston, serving over 6.1 million passengers in 2023, its busiest year on record. It is a focus city for Breeze Airways.

The military relationship is unusual and worth understanding. Joint Base Charleston owns and operates the runways, and the civilian airport uses them under a joint-use agreement with the Charleston County Aviation Authority. The site is divided into four areas: military to the west, the airline terminal to the south, general aviation to the east and the Boeing plant further south.

That Boeing plant is where the 787 Dreamliner is assembled, which brings a steady stream of business travel through the airport.

Two runways serve the combined 2,060 acre site, the longer at 9,001 feet.
after:
South Carolina's busiest airport, about 12 miles north west of downtown Charleston. It handled about 6.3 million passengers in 2025. Breeze Airways has a base here and has flown from Charleston since 2021.

It is a joint civil and military airport. Joint Base Charleston, part of the US Air Force, owns and operates the runways. The Charleston Regional Aviation Authority runs the civilian terminal under a joint-use agreement with the base.

Two runways serve the combined 2,060 acre site, the longer at 9,001 feet.

claims.note: The FAA's table is in rank order: Charleston is 57th in the US with 3,142,402 enplanements in 2025, ahead of every other South Carolina airport (Myrtle Beach 81st, Greenville-Spartanburg 89th, Columbia 126th, Hilton Head 220th, Florence 337th).

claims.inAfter: It handled about 6.3 million passengers in 2025.
claims.note: Was 'over 6.1 million passengers in 2023, its busiest year on record'. TOTAL passengers, arriving plus departing, from the operator's calendar-year 2025 operations summary: 3,167,903 enplaned plus 3,173,242 deplaned = 6,341,145 (the sum is ours; the summary gives the two halves). The same method gives 6,153,540 for 2023, matching Wikipedia's 'over 6.1 million', and 6,295,439 for 2024, so 2025 is higher than both, though no source found calls it a record in words, so the text does not. The FAA's preliminary CY2025 table counts 3,142,402 enplanements (boardings only, about half of total passengers), in line with the operator's enplaned figure.

claims.inAfter: The Charleston Regional Aviation Authority runs the civilian terminal under a joint-use agreement with the base.
claims.note: Was 'the civilian airport uses them under a joint-use agreement with the Charleston County Aviation Authority', which named the wrong party and an old name. The agreement is between the base and the authority, and the authority now calls itself the Charleston Regional Aviation Authority: its own board page names Helen Hill chair of the Charleston County Aviation Authority from 2019 'a position she still holds today', and its June 2026 release calls her Chair of the Charleston Regional Aviation Authority. The FAA record carries both names, the newer in its latest remark. The date of the change was not found.
